local_scans.notes: p_type is dict-encoded uint8 (150 entries, 25 start with PROMO). p_partkey is dense [1,2000000].

operators.description: Load p_type dict codes into uint8 direct_array[2000001] indexed by p_partkey. Pre-compute a 150-bit promo_bitset where bit i is set iff dict entry i starts with 'PROMO'.

operators.notes: Shared scan covers [1995-01-01, 1996-12-31]. Residual narrows to [1995-09-01, 1995-10-01). Dates stored as int32 YYYYMMDD.

operators.description: For each row surviving residual filter: (a) lookup type_code = type_array[l_partkey], (b) compute revenue = l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount), (c) accumulate total_sum += revenue, (d) if promo_bitset[type_code] then promo_sum += revenue. Thread-local double accumulators, no hash table needed.

accumulators.name: promo_sum
accumulators.expr: CASE WHEN promo_bitset[type_array[l_partkey]] THEN l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount) ELSE 0 END

operators.notes: Fuse join lookup + conditional aggregation into single pass. No materialization of join result. Direct array lookup is O(1) with perfect cache behavior for sequential partkeys.

operators.description: Merge thread-local (promo_sum, total_sum) pairs. Compute promo_revenue = 100.0 * promo_sum / total_sum.

parallelism.scope: step 2+3 fused: parallel morsels over shared scan output; step 1: single-thread load (2MB, trivial); step 4: single-thread merge

notes: Extremely lightweight tail. The key optimization is fusing the join and aggregation: since we only need p_type to decide promo vs non-promo, we store just the uint8 dict code in a direct array (2MB, fits in L3 cache). The PROMO check becomes a bitset test on 150 entries. No hash table, no materialized join output. The entire tail is a single streaming pass over ~783K rows with O(1) lookups.
